title: Alternative Fuel System — Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (P25A4)
shortDescription: Alternative fuel / flex-fuel system fault: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range/Performance. Stored as P25A4.
fullDescription: Flex-fuel and alternative-fuel vehicles (E85 ethanol, biodiesel, CNG, LPG) rely on a fuel composition sensor to measure the alcohol/biodiesel ratio so the PCM can adapt injector pulse width, spark timing, and cold-start enrichment. Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range/Performance indicates the PCM detected an out-of-range, implausible, or unreliable signal from the composition sensor circuit, the alternative-fuel level/quality sensor, or the related ethanol learning routine.
safetyImpact: Driveable in most cases; expect cold-start hesitation, reduced fuel economy, and possible misfire on high-ethanol blends.

causes.cause: Failed flex-fuel composition sensor
Contaminated or out-of-spec fuel (water, low-grade biodiesel)
Wiring or connector fault between fuel sensor and PCM
Fuel-rail pressure deviation affecting composition learn
PCM software update required for new fuel blend

symptoms: Hard cold start on E85 or biodiesel

fixSteps.title: Verify Fuel Quality
fixSteps.instruction: Drain a sample and test ethanol/biodiesel content with a refractometer or alcohol-content tool.

fixSteps.title: Scan Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Read fuel composition PID and compare against actual blend; values should track within 5 percent.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor connector for 5V reference, ground, and frequency signal at idle.

fixSteps.title: Replace Composition Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Composition sensor is inline on the fuel supply; depressurize rail before replacement.

faq.q: Can I keep running E85?
faq.a: Switch to straight gasoline until repaired so the PCM can use a default blend assumption.

faq.q: Will biodiesel above B20 cause this?
faq.a: Yes — many factory composition sensors are not validated above B20 and will flag implausible signals.
